title: Forecasting Bitcoin volatility spikes from whale transactions and CryptoQuant data using Synthesizer Transformer models

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper proposes a deep learning Synthesizer Transformer model to forecast next-day extreme Bitcoin volatility spikes using CryptoQuant on-chain/exchange metrics and Twitter whale-alert transaction data. Standardized features and technical indicators are fed into decoder-only transformer variants with synthetic attention mechanisms (dense, random, factorized, and mixed). Models are evaluated via regression (RMSE) and binary classification (F1-score, precision, recall) against baselines like LSTM, Vanilla Transformer, and GARCH, and subsequently tested using backtested trading strategies with volatility-scaled position sizing.
key_findings: Synthesizer Transformer models outperform traditional baseline models like LSTM, Vanilla Transformer, and GARCH in forecasting extreme Bitcoin volatility spikes.
The Synthesizer Transformer with factorized dense attention (FD) achieves the best performance with an RMSE of 0.101 and an F1-score of 0.463.
Explainable AI analysis via Captum reveals that features such as taker_buy_volume, HL_spread, volume, exchange_outflow_mean_ma7, and whale USDminus significantly influence volatility predictions.

Backtesting simple trading strategies demonstrates that integrating volatility predictions combined with volatility scaling can enhance Sharpe ratios and total returns while mitigating downside drawdowns.
limitations: The trading strategies evaluated are simple and serve primarily to show the usefulness of predictions rather than being fully optimized real-world strategies.
The dataset relies on out-of-time test splitting due to deep learning data requirements rather than continuous rolling time frames.
